findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:2446 — Terminal retention GC permanently invalidates already-imported managed review evidence. pruneExpiredManagedHostRuns() archives the receipt and then calls removeManagedHostRunRuntime(), deleting the run directory. managedHostRunReceipt() has an archive fallback, but verifyManagedReviewEvidence() (packages/main/src/core/managed-review-evidence.ts:186-238) additionally calls readManagedHostRunBinding() (reads spec.json + owner.json) and digests terminal.json, evidence-proposal.json, spec.json and events.jsonl from that same deleted directory. Empirically verified: after removeManagedHostRunRuntime(), readManagedHostRunBinding() throws ENOENT. Verification then returns the F-107/F-120 fail-closed refusal; the REVIEW gate (packages/main/src/core/review-run.ts:1527-1556) maps it to managed_receipt_invalid, which is absent from SUPERSEDED_PASS_ISSUE_CODES (review-run.ts:130-139), so it reaches evidenceState.invalid and hard-blocks REVIEW->TEST before the blocking-severity filter — the same mechanism documented in the F-100 comment. This contradicts docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:229-238, which promises GC 'preserves the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding digest' for audit, so it is a behavior/doc gap rather than an intended trade-off. Existing coverage asserts the receipt 'remains auditable after heavy runtime GC' (packages/main/src/tasks/managed-host-run-smoke.ts:1128) but never re-runs verifyManagedReviewEvidence() post-GC, which is why it was not caught. Suggested fix: give verifyManagedReviewEvidence() the same archive-backed fallback as managedHostRunReceipt() (persist the binding projection and sealed digests into the receipt archive), and extend the post-GC smoke to re-verify imported evidence.

readManifest.scanEscalationReason: Diff spans ~146 files and ~183k inserted lines, far beyond bounded full-read capacity. Full reads were spent on the four new/most security-critical production modules; the remaining large files (managed-host-run.ts at 2459 lines, review-run.ts, finding-verify.ts, smoke suites) were triaged by targeted grep/sed on the specific symbols and call chains under review, plus empirical execution against the built dist to confirm the reported defect.
